fieldValues.title: What the visual essay editor supports
fieldValues.decision_question: Which formatting should the visual essay editor support, out of everything the core renderer can show?
fieldValues.context: The owner, 2026-11-06 (vignette cca0ff96): 'Can we limit what is supported? I'm not sure we are ready to add image support at the moment. That may come later.' The core renders CommonMark plus tables and strikethrough, including images and rules. Finding e640280f: paragraphs containing something off the list are caught and open as source with content intact. Use in the 87 real essay paragraphs: 10 contain a heading, 4 bold, 3 a bullet list, 1 a numbered list, 1 a quote, 1 italic, 1 code, and none a link, table or image; that is a small corpus of mostly plain prose, by few writers, so it shows little about what a new writer will reach for. Precedent consulted: the owner's vignette; abed4266 (the essay package can grow basic building blocks for structured writing, which is a reason not to fake structure with formatting). Placement: the editor group's log, domain Evidence-backed writing. Sub-question for the sitting: headings. An essay's structure comes from titled, nested paragraphs, so a heading inside a paragraph may compete with it; but headings are the most used formatting in the corpus, and removing the button does not remove them from the source.
fieldValues.friction: Installing everything the renderer supports commits us to images and tables before we are ready, and every extra element is more to test on touch and in the keyboard path.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Allowlist: bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, code blocks, headings, bullet and numbered lists, quotes, links, line breaks (recommended). For: covers everything the corpus uses and what a writer would expect of a basic toolbar; images and tables can be added later by installing an extension. Against: a paragraph with a table, image or rule must be edited as source.
B. The same without headings. For: leaves structure to titled, nested paragraphs. Against: 10 of 87 real paragraphs contain a heading, and they would open as source or lose visual editing.
C. Add tables. For: they are in the cheat-sheet and used in the handbook. Against: more to build and test, poor on a phone, and no essay in the corpus uses one.
D. Everything the renderer supports, images included. For: no paragraph falls back to source. Against: the owner is not ready for images, which also raises attachment and hosting questions.
E. Inline formatting only. For: smallest; the corpus is mostly plain prose. Against: the 11 of 87 real paragraphs with headings, lists or quotes would open as source.
fieldValues.key_requirements: Cover what real essays use; no images for now; content outside the list must stay intact and editable as source; adding later should be cheap. The markdown editor keeps everything the renderer supports, because the renderer is shared and unchanged.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The visual essay editor supports only emphasis, code, headings, lists, quotes, links and line breaks, and everything else is edited as source.
fieldValues.rationale: It covers what essays use and what a writer expects of a basic toolbar, and the owner is not ready for images. The source editor keeps every other construct safe, so a short list costs little.
fieldValues.revisit_when: Writers ask for images or tables in essays, or a noticeable share of real paragraphs open as source because of something off the list.
